Streaming Background Parity — Diagnosis & Fix

Why the batch-optimized (decode-once streaming) tracker deviated from the pre-optimization tracker, how the deviation was traced to the ROI background model, and the three-iteration fix that restored parity. Evidence is from 8 real localsearch clips (2176×2176, 4 arenas, ~18 000 frames, 20 fps) on an Apple M3 Pro.

Analysis date: 2026-07-04 · companion to optimization_planning.html, pipeline.html & background_methods.html
TL;DR. The streaming path fit each ROI's GMM background from the first 100 consecutive frames. In a localsearch assay the fly often sits still at the start, so it got baked into the background and the tracker lost it — producing centroid errors of tens to hundreds of pixels (median 26.6 px vs the reference tracker), not the sub-pixel differences expected. The fix samples the background uniformly across the whole video and decodes those samples through the same FFmpeg crop→scale→gray filter the tracker uses. Result: median error 26.6 → 1.53 px, worst-case cells halved, and no cleanly-tracked cell regressed. Two earlier fix attempts each looked good on aggregate but silently broke individual arenas — caught only by checking tracks against the raw video.

1 · Setup & the symptom

Three tracks datasets were compared over the same 8-video batch, all at default config (roi_downscale = 2, gmm_n_samples = 100):

LabelVersionROI background source
preoptpre-optimization (file path)per-ROI GMM on the downscaled ROI video, frames sampled uniformly across the clip
currentbatch-optimized (decode-once streaming)GMM on the first 100 consecutive streamed frames
stride2streaming + --stride 2same as current (background unchanged; only every 2nd frame tracked)

Comparison metric: per-(roi, frame) centroid distance between two datasets (one track per arena, so alignment is exact), summarized as RMSE / p95 / max in full-frame pixels. The expectation from prior matrix work was sub-pixel differences. Instead current vs preopt showed a median RMSE of 26.6 px, with 18 of 32 arena-cells above 20 px and several in the hundreds. stride2 tracked current almost exactly — so the stride was not the cause; the streaming background was.

The large-error frames shared two tells: the fly was stationary (speed ≈ 0) and the two versions reported a different number of detection candidates — i.e. they were seeing different blobs, which means the background subtraction differed.

2 · Root cause: first-100-frames vs uniform background

The two versions build the per-ROI GMM background from different frames:

  • preopt — sample_frames_uniformly() → np.linspace(0, N-1, 100): 100 frames spread across the whole 15-min clip. A moving fly appears in a different place in each sample, so the per-pixel GMM mode is the empty arena → the fly is correctly excluded from the background.
  • current (streaming) — a FIFO can't seek, so the worker buffers the first 100 consecutive frames (~5 s) and fits the GMM on those (tracking_fast.py, streaming worker).

In a localsearch assay the fly is placed and often sits still for the opening seconds. If it is stationary during those first 100 frames, it occupies the same pixels in every sample → it becomes the dominant per-pixel mode → it is baked into the background. Where the fly was baked in, background subtraction returns ≈ 0, so the fly is invisible and the tracker latches onto reflections, edge glare, or a second dark object — and, having no re-identification, stays there for thousands of frames.

A statistical check across all 32 cells confirmed the mechanism: cells with RMSE > 20 px had a median fly motion of just 3.8 px during the first-100-frame window (essentially pinned), while cells with RMSE < 5 px had a median motion of 84 px (the fly was already moving, so it was never baked in).

3 · Three deviation mechanisms

Classifying each cell by the fly's motion during the warm-up window versus the whole video separates the deviation into three regimes — all rooted in the same background difference:

Mechanismcellsmedian RMSEWhat happens
STATIONARY-ALL3148 px Fly sits still the whole video → baked into both backgrounds → both versions latch onto an edge/reflection ambiguity and disagree. Inherent, not curable by the background.
BAKED-IN-CLEAN1033 px Fly pinned at the start, roams later → baked into the first-100 background only → current mis-tracks while preopt is fine. This is what the fix targets.
MOVING-START199 px Fly already moving during warm-up → background fine → mostly accurate. The few outliers fall into the STATIONARY-ALL ambiguity.

4 · The fix — three iterations

The goal: give the streaming path the same background preopt uses (uniform, no bake-in) without giving up decode-once streaming. It took three tries, and each intermediate version taught something the aggregate numbers hid.

v1 — reuse the cropped full-frame GMM rejected

The pipeline already builds a uniform-sampled full-frame background for ROI detection. v1 cropped that per ROI and reused it. Aggregate improved (median 26.6 → 6.8 px), but checking tracks against the raw video revealed it silently broke cells that current tracked fine.

v2 — per-ROI uniform GMM, cv2 downscaling closer, still flawed

v2 sampled the whole video uniformly, cropped + downscaled each sample per ROI, then fit the GMM — fixing the downscale-order problem and the bake-in (median → 1.91 px, and v1's worst regression 263 → 1.35 px). But two cells current tracked cleanly were still broken (11_16_39 arena_02: 24 → 552 px). The remaining culprit: the samples were downscaled with cv2 INTER_AREA, but the streaming frames are downscaled by FFmpeg. The two scalers disagree at the arena rim:

cv2 vs FFmpeg background, 11_16_39 arena_02: mean |difference| — interior 1.8, rim band 2.2; pixels differing by > 15 gray levels: interior 0, rim 420 (max 74). Those 420 rim pixels are false-foreground candidates that pin the tracker whenever a fly starts or passes near the boundary — exactly the two cells that regressed.

v3 — per-ROI uniform GMM, FFmpeg-sampled shipped

v3 samples the background through the same FFmpeg split → crop → scale → gray filter the tracker uses, with a select that keeps every N-th frame across the whole video (one extra decode pass). The background pixels are now bit-for-bit consistent with the tracked pixels, and sampled uniformly. On the exact cell v1/v2 failed, v3 tracks the real fly, matching preopt:

VersionROI backgroundmedianmean> 2 px> 20 px

Safety property. Every cell that current tracked cleanly (< 5 px) stays < 5 px under v3 — the fix never breaks a good track. v1 and v2 both violated this (v1 broke a 2.7 px cell to 263 px; v2 broke a 24 px cell to 552 px), which is why the video check was essential and why v3 is the version that ships.

6 · What the fix cannot solve — inherent ambiguity

Eight cells stay above 20 px under every version. These are the STATIONARY-ALL / ambiguous arenas: a fly that barely moves, near an edge, with a competing dark blob (a second object, a reflection, or persistent debris baked into every background). The centroid tracker has no appearance model and no re-identification, so its choice between two near-equivalent blobs is chaotically sensitive to any perturbation. In these cells:

  • preopt is not ground truth. It is one arbitrary outcome of a chaotic tie-break; current, v2 and v3 each pick differently. Reducing "RMSE vs preopt" there is not even the right objective.
  • They must be resolved by watching the video (a QC overlay), not by comparing to a reference dataset.
  • The durable fix is tracker robustness — a motion/appearance model or re-ID so a stationary, edge-adjacent fly isn't handed off to a reflection — not a background change. This is the recommended follow-up.

7 · What changed & how to reproduce

FileChange
preprocess.pynew build_roi_backgrounds_uniform() — one FFmpeg pass, select every N-th frame, same split→crop→scale→gray filter as the tracking stream, per-ROI GMM fit; falls back to None on any error (worker then builds its own GMM).
run.pybuild the per-ROI uniform backgrounds and pass them as roi_backgrounds to the tracking session (replacing the crop-full-frame-GMM path).
config.pybg_reuse_for_roi default False → True.

Reproduce the comparison: track a directory with the pre-optimization commit in a git worktree and with the current checkout into separate output dirs, then align tracks on (roi, frame) and report per-cell centroid RMSE. For the disputed cells, overlay each version's claimed position on the raw video frames — the RMSE-vs-reference number is necessary but not sufficient to decide which track is right.
